title: Classical diagonal-information benchmark
label: prop:diagonal_minimax
statement:
\label{prop:diagonal_minimax}
Assume \eqref{eq:model}, \eqref{eq:equalL} and $0<\alpha<1/4$. For each integer $1\le s\le p$, put
\[
 b_s=\min\left\{M s^{-K/2},\
       \tau\sqrt{\log\left(1+\frac{p}{4s^2}\right)}\right\},
 \qquad
 c_{\alpha,d}=1-2\alpha-\frac12\sqrt{e^{1/4}-1}>0.
\]
Every $C\in\mathcal C_{\alpha,d}(\Theta_1)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:diagonal_lower}
 \E_0|C|\ge c_{\alpha,d}\frac{s b_s}{\sqrt p}.
\end{equation}
For fixed $K\ge3$ and $M=\tau\sqrt p$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:diagonal_rate}
 \mathcal L_{0,d}(\Theta_1)\asymp
 \mathcal L_{\max,d}(\Theta_1)\asymp
 \tau\left(\frac{\log p}{p}\right)^{(K-2)/(2K)}.
\end{equation}
The comparison constants depend on $K$ and $\alpha$.

label: thm:harmonic

title: Sparse harmonic lower bound
label: thm:sparse_harmonic
statement:
\label{thm:sparse_harmonic}
Under \eqref{eq:model} and \eqref{eq:equalL}, let $K=3$ and $0<\alpha<1/4$.
For every integer $1\le m\le p$, put
\[
 b_m=\min\left\{\frac{M}{\sqrt{27m}},
       \frac{\tau}{\sqrt{27}}\sqrt{\log(1+p/(4m^2))}\right\},
 \qquad c_{\alpha,d}=1-2\alpha-\tfrac12\sqrt{e^{1/4}-1}.
\]
Every interval honest on a class containing the rank-one Frobenius ball satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sparse_harmonic}
 \E_0|C|\ge c_{\alpha,d}\frac{b_mH_m}{\sqrt p}.
\end{equation}
If $M=\tau\sqrt p$, then for $p\ge256$ and $m=\lfloor p^{1/4}\rfloor$,
\[
 \E_0|C|\ge\frac{c_{\alpha,d}}{16\sqrt{27}}\,
                  \frac{\tau(\log p)^{3/2}}{\sqrt p}.
\]

title: Uniform diameter and full-data minimax length
label: thm:full_minimax

title: Squared-error consequence
label: prop:mse_sharp
statement:
\label{prop:mse_sharp}
In the regime of \eqref{eq:full_rates},
\[
 \inf_{\widehat\psi}\sup_{A\in\Theta}
          \E_A(\widehat\psi-\psi(A))^2\asymp r_K(p)^2.
\]
The midpoint of $C_F$ with error level $\alpha_p=p^{-2}$ attains the upper order for $p\ge2$.

title: Truncated scans
label: prop:truncated
statement:
\label{prop:truncated}
For $1\le t\le p$, test zero using only supports of sizes at most $t$, retaining thresholds calibrated simultaneously over all sizes. Write $\lambda_s=\lambda_s(\gamma)$ and put
\[
 q=2/K,\quad B_q=J^{1-1/K}M^q,\quad
 a_t=4J^{K/2}\lambda_t t^{-K/2},
\]
\[
 R_t=\frac{4J^{K/2}}{\sqrt p}\sum_{s=1}^t\lambda_s s^{-K/2}
       +\mathbf1_{\{t<p\}}\frac{B_q}{\sqrt p}a_t^{1-q}.
\]
On acceptance use radius $\min(h_0,R_t)$ centered at zero; on rejection use the structural interval.
Intersect with $C_*(\alpha_0)$, where $0<\alpha_0,\gamma<1$,
$\alpha_0+\gamma\le\alpha$, and $\gamma$ is the scan error budget, using the singleton convention.
The resulting $C_t$ is honest, has length at most $\ell_*=|C_*(\alpha_0)|$, and
\[
 \E_0|C_t|\le\min(\ell_*,2R_t+\ell_*\gamma).
\]
For fixed $K\ge3$, fixed caps and fixed $0<\alpha<1$, with $M=\tau\sqrt p$, $\alpha_0=\alpha/2$ and $\gamma=\alpha/(2p)$,
\begin{align}\label{eq:trunc_rate}
 R_t\lesssim{}&
 \frac{\tau\sqrt{\log p}}{\sqrt p}
       \sum_{s=1}^t s^{-(K-1)/2}\\
 &+\mathbf1_{\{t<p\}}\tau(\log p/p)^\beta
                t^{-(K-1)\beta},\qquad
 \beta=(K-2)/(2K).\nonumber
\end{align}

title: A low-degree estimation separation
label: thm:low_degree
statement:
\label{thm:low_degree}
Let $K\ge3$, $1\le s\le\sqrt p$, and mix uniformly over
\[
 x_S=s^{-1/2}\mathbf1_S,\qquad
 A_S=\tau\lambda x_S^{\otimes K},\qquad |S|=s.
\]
Assume $0<\tau\lambda\le M$, and write
\[
 \delta=\frac{\tau\lambda s^{1-K/2}}{\sqrt p},\quad
 \mu=s^2/p,\quad B_D=\frac{\lambda^2}{s^K}(KD)^K,
\]
where $D\ge1$ is the polynomial degree. If $B_D<1$, the centered likelihood ratio projected onto polynomials of degree at most $D$ has squared null norm at most
\[
 \eta_D^2=\mu e^\mu B_D/(1-B_D).
\]
Every scalar polynomial estimator $T(Z)$ of degree at most $D$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lowdegree_risk}
 \sup_{A\in\Theta}\E_A(T-\psi(A))^2
       \ge\frac{\delta^2}{(2+\eta_D)^2}
\end{equation}
on any parameter class containing zero and these alternatives.
In particular, let $M=\tau\sqrt p$, $\lambda=\sqrt p$,
$s=\lfloor p^a\rfloor$, and $D=\lfloor p^b\rfloor$, where
\[
 \frac1K<a<\min\left(\frac12,\frac1{K-2}\right),
 \qquad 0<b<a-\frac1K.
\]
Then $\eta_D\to0$ and the lower order in \eqref{eq:lowdegree_risk} is polynomially larger than the unrestricted rate in Proposition~\ref{prop:mse_sharp}.

title: What an efficient short interval would imply
label: prop:ci_detection
statement:
\label{prop:ci_detection}
Let $Q$ be supported on parameters with common target $\delta>0$, and let the null target be zero.
An interval honest at level $1-\alpha$ at the null and these alternatives defines
$\phi(Z)=\mathbf1\{\delta\in C(Z)\}$ with
\[
 Q(\phi=0)\le\alpha,\qquad
 P_0(\phi=1)\le\alpha+\E_0|C|/\delta.
\]
A computational hypothesis excluding polynomial-time tests with total error below $c>2\alpha$ therefore excludes polynomial-time honest intervals with
$\E_0|C|<(c-2\alpha)\delta$ for that prior.

title: Diameter using both norm and scan constraints
label: thm:norm_diameter
statement:
\label{thm:norm_diameter}
For every $p\ge1$, $K\ge3$, $M,\tau>0$ and $0<\alpha<1$, the residual-projection interval $C_F$ is honest and satisfies, for every observation,
\[
 |C_F|\le\min\{2h_0,U_{K,p}(M;\alpha)\}.
\]
The bound retains the supplied norm budget inside the ordered-coordinate sum; taking the minimum only after summation can lose the intermediate cubic regime.

title: Full-data length for every positive norm budget
label: thm:all_norm_rates
statement:
\label{thm:all_norm_rates}
Fix $K\ge3$, positive Tucker or TT caps, and $0<\alpha<1/4$. For the equal diagonal contrast there are constants $0<c<C<\infty$, depending only on these fixed quantities, such that for every $p\ge1$ and every $M,\tau>0$,
\[
 c\,\mathfrak r_K(p,M,\tau)
 \le\mathcal L_0(\Theta)
 \le\mathcal L_{\max}(\Theta)
 \le C\,\mathfrak r_K(p,M,\tau).
\]
The lower bounds already hold when the honesty class is restricted to rank-one tensors. The interval in Theorem~\ref{thm:norm_diameter} attains the upper order.

title: Squared risk uniformly over norm budgets
label: thm:all_norm_mse
statement:
\label{thm:all_norm_mse}
Under the fixed-order, fixed-cap conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:all_norm_rates},
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\psi}\sup_{A\in\Theta}
       \E_A(\widetilde\psi-\psi(A))^2
       \asymp\mathfrak r_K(p,M,\tau)^2
\]
uniformly over $p\ge1$ and $M,\tau>0$. The measurable estimator in \eqref{eq:residual_fit} attains the upper bound. It uses neither a failure probability depending on $M$ nor a minimum nonzero singular value.

title: Loading-dependent full-data bounds
label: thm:weighted_bounds
statement:
\label{thm:weighted_bounds}
For fixed $K\ge3$, fixed positive caps and fixed $0<\alpha<1/4$, an honest interval obtained by residual projection in the rotated block satisfies
\[
 |C_w(Z)|\le\min(2h_0,U_w)
\]
for every observation. Conversely every interval honest on the full ambient cap class satisfies
\[
 \E_0|C(Z)|\ge c_{K,\alpha}L_w.
\]
The lower bound allows use of every ambient tensor entry. These bounds are not asserted to match for arbitrary nonuniform weights.

title: Sharp rates for a flat orthogonal loading
label: prop:flat_loading
statement:
\label{prop:flat_loading}
If $w_i=\epsilon_i/\sqrt m$ with prescribed $\epsilon_i\in\{-1,1\}$, then both minimax expected-length criteria have order $\mathfrak r_K(m,M,\tau)$, and minimax squared error has its square, independently of the larger ambient mode dimensions. The statement includes dense orthogonal rotations of the loading. At $m=1$ it gives the bounded-normal-mean scale $\min(M,\tau)$.

title: Full-data robustness under directional tails
label: thm:sg_full
statement:
\label{thm:sg_full}
In $Z=A+E$, replace $\tau$ by a known $v>0$ in the scan thresholds and residual-fit tolerance. Under \eqref{eq:joint_sg}, the norm-sensitive diameter, uniform squared-risk upper bound, and orthogonal-loading upper bounds remain valid. For fixed order/caps, their equal-diagonal orders are $\mathfrak r_K(p,M,v)$ and its square. If the noise law is an unknown member of the family satisfying \eqref{eq:joint_sg}, these rates are minimax when coverage and the supremum risk/length range over that family. This lower-bound statement need not hold for each fixed non-Gaussian law separately.

title: Full scans with only finite-variance replicates
label: thm:mom_full
statement:
\label{thm:mom_full}
Use the feasible constraints
$|d_U-\ip UB|\le\lambda_s^{\rm mom}$ in place of the Gaussian residual constraints. Their projection onto the equal-diagonal target is honest at level $1-\beta$, with the norm-sensitive diameter using $\lambda_s^{\rm mom}$. For fixed $K$, caps and confidence, both minimax expected-length criteria, with a supremum over all the stated replicate laws, have order $\mathfrak r_K(p,M,\sigma/\sqrt n)$ whenever \eqref{eq:mom_blocks} holds.

For squared error use $\beta=1/8$ and approximately minimize
\[
 F(B)=\max\bigl(0,\max_U\{|d_U-\ip UB|-\lambda_{s(U)}^{\rm mom}\}\bigr)
\]
over a fixed countable dense cap-class sequence, within tolerance $\tau$. The resulting scalar estimator has minimax squared risk of order $\mathfrak r_K^2$ over the same family. This is an existence construction. The sufficient replicate count is $n\ge C_{K,\beta}p$, and the full directional search remains exponential.

title: Two limits of a noise relaxation
label: prop:noise_limits

title: Sharp length under a Frobenius approximation allowance
label: thm:approx_sharp
statement:
\label{thm:approx_sharp}
In the original Gaussian experiment let
$\Theta^\eta=\Theta(M,\bar r)+\eta\mathbb B_F$, $\eta\ge0$. For the equal diagonal, fixed $K\ge3$, fixed positive caps and fixed $0<\alpha<1/4$,
\[
 \mathcal L_0(\Theta^\eta)\asymp\mathcal L_{\max}(\Theta^\eta)
 \asymp \min\{\tau,\mathfrak r_K(p,M,\tau)+\eta\}.
\]
The upper interval inflates every scan threshold by $\eta$ and both projected endpoints by $\eta$, with a deterministically selected direct Gaussian fallback. Thus approximate low rank is allowed, but the original rate requires $\eta=O(\mathfrak r_K)$.

title: A growing-rank lower bound and the unrestricted endpoint
label: prop:growing_caps

title: A confidence interval for any certified loading decomposition
label: prop:loading_transfer
statement:
\label{prop:loading_transfer}
Suppose $C_0=[a_0,b_0]$ is honest for $\ip{L_0}A$ at error $\alpha_0$, and
$\PP(|\ip RE|>q_R)\le\alpha_1$ uniformly. Then
\[
 C_L=[a_0+\ip RZ-q_R,\ b_0+\ip RZ+q_R]
\]
is honest at error $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ and has length $|C_0|+2q_R$.
Under \eqref{eq:joint_sg}, one may take
\[
 q_R=v\norm R_F\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha_1)}.
\]
For Gaussian noise use the normal quantile. No independence between the two terms is required. A decomposition or partition selected from loading and supplied constants alone needs no selection penalty. Selection using $Z$ does require simultaneous calibration.

This also supplies additional unequal-weight upper bounds: partition the orthogonal terms into prescribed blocks, apply their separate weighted bounds with error budgets summing to $\alpha$, and add the intervals. Include the unsplit construction among the choices. The minimum among their deterministic diameter bounds is achievable by choosing the construction before observing data.

title: Two efficiently attained minimax regimes
label: thm:efficient_regimes
statement:
\label{thm:efficient_regimes}
(i) For the equal diagonal, fixed order/caps and $M\le\tau\sqrt{\log(ep)}$, the structural interval is minimax up to fixed constants, with length of order $M/\sqrt p$.
(ii) Let a parameter class contained in $\{A:\norm A_F\le M\}$ contain every rank-one tensor of Frobenius norm at most $M$. If a supplied unit product tensor $U$ certifies
$|\ip LU|\ge c\norm L_F$ for a fixed $c>0$, then under Gaussian observations both length criteria have order $\norm L_F\min(M,\tau)$. Choose between the norm-only structural interval and the direct Gaussian interval. The algorithm uses a contraction and scalar comparisons, without rank recovery or tensor optimization. This covers arbitrary loadings with a certified constant product overlap, regardless of supplied rank caps.

title: Why full convexification loses the weak-signal gain
label: prop:convex_loss
statement:
\label{prop:convex_loss}
Any convex parameter set containing the rank-one Frobenius ball of radius $M$ also contains $\{tL:|t|\le M/\sqrt p\}$ for the equal diagonal loading. Consequently, every interval honest on that convex set satisfies
\[
 \E_0|C|\ge c_\alpha\min(M/\sqrt p,\tau).
\]
At $M=\tau\sqrt p$ this is order $\tau$, exceeding the original full-data rate by an unbounded factor as $p\to\infty$. The conclusion concerns procedures guaranteeing coverage on the whole convex outer class; it is not a computational lower bound for every algorithm using a convex subroutine.

title: An adaptation obstruction at nonzero tensors
label: thm:shifted_adaptation
statement:
\label{thm:shifted_adaptation}
Suppose $A_0$ is supported on $\{1,\ldots,q\}^K$, $q<p$, has norm $a<M$, and every supplied unfolding cap is at least its actual rank plus one. Put $m=p-q$ and $M_0=(M^2-a^2)^{1/2}$. For the equal diagonal every interval honest on the outer cap class satisfies
\[
 \E_{A_0}|C|\ge c_{K,\alpha}\sqrt{m/p}\,
           \mathfrak r_K(m,M_0,\tau).
\]
Thus arbitrarily weak extra components obstruct shortening at some nonzero lower-rank tensors, not only at zero. This is a lower bound, not a complete characterization of adaptation on all rank subclasses.

title: Finite-sample rank calibration with a computable bias correction
label: thm:adaptive_tangent

title: Controlled squared component weights
label: lem:cp
statement:
\label{lem:cp}
For a tensor in either cap class there is a finite representation
\[
 A=\sum_{j=1}^{J_A}x_{1j}\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{Kj},\qquad
 a_j^{\mathrm{cp}}=\prod_{k=1}^K\norm{x_{kj}}_2,
\]
such that $J_A\le J$ and $\sum_j(a_j^{\mathrm{cp}})^2=\norm A_F^2$.

title: Exact diagonal reduction
label: lem:image
statement:
\label{lem:image}
Under \eqref{eq:loading}, the image of the rank-one tensor Frobenius ball of radius $M$ under $A\mapsto(\ip A{V_i})_{i=1}^m$ is exactly
\[
 \left\{a\in\R^m:\sum_i|a_i|^{2/K}\le M^{2/K}\right\}.
\]

title: Scalar threshold envelope
label: lem:soft
statement:
\label{lem:soft}
If $|e|\le\lambda$ and $s=\soft_\lambda(x+e)$, then $s$ lies between zero and $x$ and
\[
 |s-x|\le\min(|x|,2\lambda).
\]
For $q\in(0,1]$, $t,u\ge0$, one also has $\min(t,u)\le t^q u^{1-q}$, with the continuous interpretation at zero.

title: Matrix functional bound
label: lem:structural
statement:
\label{lem:structural}
If $\rank(B)\le r$ and $H$ has singular values $s_1(H)\ge s_2(H)\ge\cdots$, then
\[
 |\ip HB|\le\norm B_F\left(\sum_{i\le r}s_i(H)^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]

title: Common-target alternatives
label: lem:mixture

title: Finite product nets and injective norm
label: lem:net_scan
statement:
\label{lem:net_scan}
The nets used in \eqref{eq:scan_threshold} exist and satisfy
$\rho(B)\le2N_S(B)$ for any tensor on $S^K$.
Furthermore, a tensor $B$ in either rank-cap class satisfies
$\norm B_F\le\sqrt J\,\rho(B)$.

title: Uniform cubic moment for a weighted sign sum
label: lem:cubic_moment
statement:
\label{lem:cubic_moment}
For independent uniform signs $\epsilon_i$, let
$S_p=\sum_{i=1}^p i^{-2/3}\epsilon_i$. Then, uniformly in $p\ge1$,
\[
 \PP(|S_p|>x)\le2e^{-x^3/192}\quad(x\ge12),
 \qquad
 \E\exp\{|S_p|^3/40000\}\le20/19+1/100<5/4.
\]

title: Smaller rank coefficient
label: prop:budget
statement:
\label{prop:budget}
In $\sum_i|a_i|^{2/K}\le D M^{2/K}$ one may take
\[
 D_{\Tu}=\min\left\{J_{\Tu}^{1-1/K},m^{1-1/K},
                  (\prod_k\bar r_k)^{1/K}\right\}.
\]
For TT caps put $\bar r_0=\bar r_K=1$ and
$\rho_k=\min(p_k,\bar r_{k-1}\bar r_k)$; one may take
\[
 D_{\TT}=\min\left\{J_{\TT}^{1-1/K},m^{1-1/K},
                  (\prod_k\rho_k)^{1/K}\right\}.
\]
The nonlinear radius remains valid with coefficient $D$.

title: Structural range and fixed affine optimum
label: prop:affine_exact
statement:
\label{prop:affine_exact}
The range of $\psi$ on either cap class under \eqref{eq:loading} is exactly $[-h_0,h_0]$. Under \eqref{eq:equalL} and $0<\alpha<1/2$, set
$a_0=M\sqrt{s_{\rm cap}/p}$. Among all honest full-data fixed-radius affine intervals, the optimal radius is
\[
 h_{\rm aff}^*=\min_{0\le t\le1}Q_\alpha(a_0(1-t),\tau t).
\]
Center $t\ip LZ$ attains the optimum. If $a_0\le z_{1-\alpha}\tau$, then $h_{\rm aff}^*=a_0$.

title: Envelope and approximation calibration
label: prop:envelope
statement:
\label{prop:envelope}
Suppose $d_i=a_i+e_i$ and, uniformly over the asserted class,
$\PP(\max_i|e_i|\le\lambda_0)\ge1-\alpha$.
For any measurable $\Lambda\ge\lambda_0$, the threshold center has an honest radius
\[
 \norm w_\infty D M^{2/K}(2\Lambda)^{1-2/K}+\eta
\]
on $\Theta^\eta$. The structural radius is $h_0+\eta$.
Data-dependent selection between these two intervals is valid.
A direct Gaussian alternative needs its own calibration and deterministic selection or joint error allocation.

title: Replicate median calibration
label: prop:mom
statement:
\label{prop:mom}
Let clean tensor replicates be independent with common mean $A$, and every prescribed contraction have variance at most known $v^2$. Allow at most $c$ adversarial replacements of entire replicates. Coordinates within a replicate may be dependent. Choose an odd block count $b$ with
\[
 b\ge8c,\qquad b\ge32\log(m/\alpha),\qquad n\ge2b,
 \qquad k=\lfloor n/b\rfloor.
\]
Partition the first $bk$ replicates into fixed disjoint blocks.
For coordinatewise medians $d_i$ of the block means,
\[
 \PP(\max_i|d_i-a_i|>2v/\sqrt k)\le\alpha.
\]
Thus Proposition~\ref{prop:envelope} applies. For the smallest admissible odd $b$,
the threshold has order
\[
 O\{v\sqrt{c/n+\log(m/\alpha)/n}\}.
\]

title: Independent residual calibration
label: prop:variance
statement:
\label{prop:variance}
Retain $n\ge2$ iid Gaussian full-tensor replicates with unknown noise standard deviation $\sigma>0$.
Let $d_{ji}=\ip{W_j}{V_i}$, $\bar d_i=n^{-1}\sum_jd_{ji}$, $\nu=m(n-1)$, and
\[
 S^2=\nu^{-1}\sum_i\sum_j(d_{ji}-\bar d_i)^2,\qquad
 \sigma_U=S\sqrt{\nu/\chi^2_{\nu,\delta}},\quad 0<\delta<\alpha.
\]
The denominator is the lower $\delta$ chi-square quantile.
Compute the original three intervals with $\tau_U=\sigma_U/\sqrt n$ and
$\alpha_0=\alpha-\delta$, choosing the smallest using only $S$ and supplied quantities.
The selected interval is honest at level $1-\alpha$.
For fixed $\delta$ and $\nu\to\infty$, $\sigma_U/\sigma\to1$ in probability,
and the nonlinear expected-length order is preserved.

title: Calibrated lower bounds
label: prop:levels

title: A norm-sensitive harmonic sum
label: lem:norm_sum
statement:
\label{lem:norm_sum}
For $p\ge1$, $x>0$ and $K\ge3$, put
\[
 S_{K,p}(x)=\sum_{s=1}^p\min\{x s^{-K/2},s^{-(K-1)/2}\}.
\]
Then $S_{3,p}(x)\le4g_p(x)$, and $S_{K,p}(x)\le3\min(x,1)$ for $K\ge4$.
For fixed $K$ and $0<\alpha<1$,
$U_{K,p}(M;\alpha)\le C_{K,\bar r,\alpha}\mathfrak r_K(p,M,\tau)$ uniformly in $p,M,\tau$.

title: Residual fit and its noise tail
label: lem:residual_fit
statement:
\label{lem:residual_fit}
The estimator in \eqref{eq:residual_fit} is Borel measurable. With $T_0=T(\tau G)$ and $\beta=1/8$,
\[
 \PP(T_0>t)\le\beta e^{-t^2/(2\tau^2)}\quad(t\ge0),
 \qquad \E T_0^2\le2\beta\tau^2.
\]
Put $z_K=\sum_{s=1}^{\infty}s^{-K/2}\le3$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:residual_error}
 |\widehat\psi-\psi(A)|\le U_{K,p}(M;\beta)
              +\frac{Q_2z_K}{\sqrt p}(T_0+\tau/2),
 \qquad |\widehat\psi-\psi(A)|\le2h_0.
\end{equation}

title: A quantitative contract for approximate minimax optimization
label: C1
statement:
Use every support and every direction in the calibrated finite product nets.
For their unit directions $U$ and thresholds $\lambda_{s(U)}$, put

$$F_Z(B)=\max\{0,\max_U(|\langle U,Z-B\rangle|-\lambda_{s(U)})\}.$$

This function is 1-Lipschitz in Frobenius norm. Suppose an algorithm returns
$\widehat B\in\Theta$ and numbers $l\le\inf_{B\in\Theta}F_Z(B)\le
F_Z(\widehat B)=u$, with $u-l\le\varepsilon$. On the simultaneous noise
event, the true $A$ is feasible, so $F_Z(A)=0$ and $u\le\varepsilon$.
Consequently, for every support size $s$,

$$N_S(\widehat B-A)\le 2\lambda_s+\varepsilon.$$

With $J_2=J(2\bar r)$, the preceding ordered-diagonal proof gives

$$|\widehat B_{i,\ldots,i}-A_{i,\ldots,i}|_{(s)}
\le \min\{2J_2^{(K-1)/2}M,
4J_2^{K/2}(\lambda_s+\varepsilon/2)\}s^{-K/2}.$$

For known orthogonal loading weights $w_i$, sorted by absolute value, the
sum of the right side against $w_s^*$ is an honest radius about
$\psi_L(\widehat B)$. It may be intersected with the structural range.
Choosing $\varepsilon\le c\tau$ retains the existing all-budget minimax
orders for equal/flat loadings. Indeed every $\lambda_s$ is bounded below
by a positive constant times $\tau$, so the added term changes the existing
minimum by only a fixed factor, including in the norm-limited regime.

For squared error set the scan error budget to $1/8$. If the optimizer
guarantees $\varepsilon\le c\tau$ for *every observation*, the same excess
tail proof as before applies: $F_Z(\widehat B)\le F_Z(A)+\varepsilon$ and
$N_S(\widehat B-A)\le2\lambda_s+2F_Z(A)+\varepsilon$. Thus the existing
all-budget MSE bound follows. A budget-limited run with a larger reported gap
does not establish that MSE guarantee.

**Endpoint version.** Let $\mathcal F=\{B\in\Theta:F_Z(B)=0\}$.
If certified outer endpoints enclose $\psi_L(\mathcal F)$, they define an
honest interval, even at an arbitrary computation stop. If feasible
witnesses establish each outer endpoint within $\varepsilon$ of the exact
endpoint, its length exceeds the ideal projection length by at most
$2\varepsilon$. An inner optimization solution alone does not give an
honest interval. On a certified empty feasible set use $\{0\}$, as before.

**Proof.** Lipschitzness follows from $\|U\|_F=1$, the reverse triangle
inequality, and stability of finite maxima. The objective-gap implication
uses $F_Z\ge0$. Rank caps double under subtraction; the norm budget doubles
as well. The ordered bound is exactly the earlier net comparison and
diagonal quasi-norm inequality with $2\lambda_s$ replaced by
$2\lambda_s+\varepsilon$. The Gaussian union event has probability at least
$1-\alpha$. Endpoint containment proves coverage on the same event. For
the length assertion, use an inner feasible witness at each end. The
squared-risk argument invokes the already supplied excess-tail integration,
with only its deterministic tolerance constant changed. No algorithmic
complexity conclusion follows from this contract.

title: An implemented global solver on the binary rank-one class
label: C2
statement:
For $p=2$ and any fixed order $K\ge3$, every rank-one tensor of norm at most
$M$ has a representation

$$B(a,\theta)=a\bigotimes_{k=1}^K(\cos\theta_k,\sin\theta_k),
\quad a\in[-M,M],\quad\theta_k\in[0,\pi].$$

Each vector is represented up to sign on a semicircle; the product of signs
is absorbed into $a$. The zero tensor is included. There is no grid
restriction on the parameter space.

The code includes both singleton supports and the full support. For the
latter it uses $n_K=\lceil\pi K\rceil$ equally spaced angles in $[0,\pi)$
per mode. Every unit vector is within Euclidean distance $1/(2K)$ of a net
point up to sign: its angular discrepancy modulo $\pi$ is at most
$\pi/(2n_K)$. Absolute contractions remove the signs. The same telescoping
proof therefore gives $\rho\le2N$. There are $D_1=2$ singleton directions
and $D_2=n_K^K$ full-support directions. Set

$$\lambda_s=\tau\sqrt{2\log(4D_s/\alpha)},\qquad s=1,2.$$

The sum of the two Gaussian union bounds is at most $\alpha$.

For each parameter box, exact real-arithmetic ranges of cosine and products
enclose every scanned contraction and tensor entry. If their contraction
range is $[b_U^-,b_U^+]$, then

$$l_{\rm box}=\max\{0,\max_U[
\operatorname{dist}(\langle U,Z\rangle,[b_U^-,b_U^+])-\lambda_{s(U)}]\}$$

is a lower bound for $F_Z$ throughout the box. Centers provide actual
rank-one upper witnesses. A largest-scaled-side split covers the parent
with two children. Branch and bound retains global lower and upper bounds;
the objective run ends at its requested gap or reports a budget stop.
It implements the ideal residual criterion itself on this class.

For confidence projection reject a box only when its objective lower bound
is positive. Loading-entry interval arithmetic bounds every surviving
box's target; their hull contains the ideal confidence projection. Feasible
amplitude intervals at fixed central factors supply inner witnesses. An
endpoint gap is reported only when such witnesses exist. Endpoints need
not reach a requested tolerance within a finite node budget, especially
near singular feasibility boundaries. This is recorded, not treated as a
successful exact optimization.

The code supports arbitrary loadings in the binary tensor, but caps above
one and mode dimensions above two are not implemented. Exhaustive scans
and global subdivision are exponential. Tests check range containment and
global certificates against independent finite calculations. Floating
point evaluations include conservative guards; these are numerical
certificates under the derived inequalities, not formal directed-rounding
interval proofs. The real-arithmetic method, rather than any particular
floating point tolerance, is the mathematical result.

title: Sharp small-budget rates for every loading tensor
label: L1
statement:
Define the product overlap

$$\rho(L)=\sup_{\|u_k\|_2=1}|\langle L,\bigotimes_k u_k\rangle|.$$

For fixed positive caps, fixed $0<\alpha<1/4$, arbitrary mode dimensions,
and *every* known loading tensor $L$, if $0<M\le\tau$, then

$$\mathcal L_0(\Theta;L)\asymp\mathcal L_{\max}(\Theta;L)
\asymp M\rho(L),\qquad
\inf_{\widehat\psi}\sup_\Theta\mathbb E_A
(\widehat\psi-\psi_L(A))^2\asymp M^2\rho(L)^2.$$

Constants depend only on the fixed caps/order and confidence, not on $L$
or the ambient dimensions. The zero loading has identically zero risk and
length. More generally, for all $M,\tau>0$,

$$c_\alpha\rho(L)\min(M,\tau)
\le \mathcal L_0\le\mathcal L_{\max}
\le 2\min\{\sqrt J M\rho(L),\ z_{1-\alpha/2}\tau\|L\|_F\}.$$

**Proof.** The canonical expansion and Cauchy--Schwarz give
$|\psi_L(A)|\le\rho(L)\sum_j|a_j|\le\sqrt J M\rho(L)$.
This gives a deterministic interval and the risk of estimator zero. The
direct Gaussian interval gives the other upper bound; choose between the
two using known quantities. Compactness gives a maximizing product $U$;
choose its sign so $\langle L,U\rangle=\rho(L)$. Both $0$ and $tU$ belong
to every positive cap class, for $t=\min(M,\tau)/2$. Their Gaussian total
variation is $2\Phi(t/(2\tau))-1\le2\Phi(1/4)-1<1/4$.
Honesty at both parameters implies
$\mathbb E_0|C|\ge t\rho(L)(1-2\alpha-\mathrm{TV})$.
The two-point squared-loss lower bound is a fixed positive multiple of
$t^2\rho(L)^2$: classify an estimate by its nearest target. A classification
error entails squared error at least $t^2\rho(L)^2/4$, while the sum of
the two testing errors is at least $1-\mathrm{TV}$. Therefore the larger
squared risk is at least $t^2\rho(L)^2(1-\mathrm{TV})/8$.
For $M\le\tau$ the bounds match. This proof is a direct
specialization of standard Gaussian two-point reasoning, not a novel
general inference principle.

**Limits.** Computing $\rho(L)$ for a general high-order loading is itself
a global optimization problem. A certified upper bound can replace it in
the interval; a certified product witness supplies a lower bound. Without
a constant ratio between them, an efficient sharp algorithm has not been
obtained. This theorem covers all loading tensors in the stated budget
regime; it does not characterize their larger-budget rates. The flat
loading small-budget theorem extends to $M\lesssim\tau\sqrt{\log m}$,
a larger regime than the arbitrary-loading result here.

title: An optimized common-target lower bound for unequal weights
label: L2
statement:
For an orthogonal product loading with decreasing nonzero absolute weights
$w_1\ge\cdots\ge w_m>0$, choose $d\le m$ and $0<\Delta\le Mw_d$.
For signed original weights $\widetilde w_i$, set
$A_i=(\Delta/\widetilde w_i)U_i$, $1\le i\le d$.
All alternatives have target $\Delta$, satisfy the norm budget, and have
rank one. They are orthogonal as full tensors. Let

$$v_i=\exp\{\Delta^2/(\tau^2w_i^2)\}-1,\quad
H_d(\Delta)=\sum_{i=1}^d v_i^{-1},\quad
\pi_i=v_i^{-1}/H_d(\Delta).$$

The optimal chi-square divergence among mixtures on these alternatives is

$$\chi^2(Q,P_0)=\min_{\pi\in\mathcal S_d}\sum_i\pi_i^2v_i
=H_d(\Delta)^{-1}.$$

Thus every interval honest on the full tensor class satisfies

$$\mathbb E_0|C|\ge\Delta\left[1-2\alpha-
\frac{1}{2\sqrt{H_d(\Delta)}}\right]_+.$$

**Proof.** The Gaussian likelihood identity gives overlap 1 for distinct
orthogonal alternatives and $1+v_i$ for equal alternatives. Subtracting 1
leaves $\sum\pi_i^2v_i$. Cauchy--Schwarz bounds this below by
$(\sum v_i^{-1})^{-1}$ and the displayed weights attain equality.
Apply $\mathrm{TV}\le\sqrt{\chi^2}/2$ and the common-target interval lemma.
This uses the full observation; there is no diagonal-data restriction.

`weighted_axis_lower` enumerates $d$ and uses scalar root finding for the
largest $\Delta\le Mw_d$ with $\chi^2\le1/4$. Every reported lower bound
uses the actual recomputed divergence and a feasible prior. This optimizes
the prior at each chosen target within the axis family. It is not an
optimization over all tensor alternatives. For equal weights it recovers
the one-spike logarithmic obstruction. It cannot recover the cubic
harmonic obstruction on its own and is not claimed sharp for all weights.

title: Unseparated rate adaptation across positive fixed caps
label: A1
statement:
Fix an outer positive Tucker or TT cap vector $\bar r$. Let $\mathcal R$
contain any collection of positive cap vectors componentwise below it.
For equal or flat orthogonal loadings, the *same* full-data outer-class
interval satisfies

$$\sup_{A\in\Theta(M,r)}\mathbb E_A|C_{\bar r}|
\le C_{K,\bar r,\alpha}\,\mathfrak r_K(m,M,\tau),\qquad r\in\mathcal R.$$

Every smaller class contains the rank-one ball, whose lower bound is
$c_{K,\alpha}\mathfrak r_K$. Therefore the interval is simultaneously
minimax in rate over every such class, uniformly in $m,M,\tau$, without
knowing the actual ranks or imposing singular-value separation. The
analogous MSE conclusion holds for the outer-class ideal residual fit.

**Proof.** Restrict the existing outer supremum upper bound to each subset
and apply the same rank-one lower bound inside each smaller class. No
selection step or new probability argument is required.

This observation resolves the fixed-positive-cap, rate-only statistical
adaptation question. It does not give optimal rank-dependent constants,
growing-cap rates, computation, exact-rank selection, or pointwise oracle
lengths. Rank zero must be excluded: its known-model oracle interval has
length zero, whereas outer-class honesty forces positive length at zero.
The preceding ledgers used the word adaptation broadly; these distinct
objectives must be separated.

title: A computable projection certificate without separation
label: A2
statement:
Let $Z^{(1)}=A+E^{(1)}$ and $Z^{(2)}=A+E^{(2)}$ have independent iid
Gaussian errors of known scales $\tau_1,\tau_2$. Only $\|A\|_F\le M$ is
assumed here; supplied rank caps are unnecessary. Let $0<\delta<\alpha$.
Use the simultaneous unfolding operator envelopes from the previous stage:

$$\eta_k=2\tau_1\sqrt{2\{(p_k+\prod_{l\ne k}p_l)\log9+
\log(2K/\delta)\}}.$$

On one event of probability at least $1-\delta$ all
$\|E^{(1)}_{(k)}\|_{op}\le\eta_k$. For any pilot-chosen ranks $r_k$, let
$Q_k$ project onto the first $r_k$ left singular vectors of $Z^{(1)}_{(k)}$.
Set $d_k=\sigma_{r_k+1}(Z^{(1)}_{(k)})+\eta_k$ if $r_k<p_k$, and $d_k=0$
if $Q_k=I$. Singular values beyond the matrix rank are zero. For
$P=\bigotimes_k Q_k$, decompose

$$R=(I-P)L=\sum_{k=1}^K R_k,\quad
R_k=\left[\bigotimes_{l<k}Q_l\right]\otimes(I-Q_k)
\otimes\left[\bigotimes_{l>k}I\right]L.$$

Then the observable bound

$$B=\min\left\{M\|R\|_F,\ \sum_k d_k\|(R_k)_{(k)}\|_*\right\}$$

satisfies $|\langle R,A\rangle|\le B$ on that event. The interval centered
at $\langle PL,Z^{(2)}\rangle$, with radius

$$B+z_{1-(\alpha-\delta)/2}\tau_2\|PL\|_F,$$

is honest over the whole norm ball. Any finite set of pilot-selected
projection choices can be compared by their radii on this same event;
choose the smallest before using validation data. Include $P=I$ for the
direct interval and $P=0$ for the structural interval. Intersect with
$[-M\|L\|_F,M\|L\|_F]$ and use $\{0\}$ for an empty intersection.

**Proof.** Residual SVD optimality and the triangle inequality give
$\|(I-Q_k)A_{(k)}\|_{op}\le d_k$ on the common event, even for selected
$r_k$. The definition of $R_k$ gives $(I-Q_k)(R_k)_{(k)}=(R_k)_{(k)}$.
Operator/nuclear norm duality bounds its contraction with $A$ by
$d_k\|(R_k)_{(k)}\|_*$. Sum and combine with the norm-only bound.
Conditional on the pilot, validation noise in the selected loading is
Gaussian with variance $\tau_2^2\|PL\|_F^2$. No multiplicity correction
over the candidate ranks is required: all bias certificates hold on one
uniform pilot event, and the choice precedes validation. The union bound
gives total error at most $\alpha$. Unfolding SVDs, tensor projections and
nuclear norms are polynomial in the explicit input size.

This algorithm never interprets an undetected component as identically
zero. It does not certify the actual rank. Its bias term can be large,
and no weak-signal or pointwise minimax optimality is claimed. Honesty on
the full norm ball cannot yield the low-rank weak-signal minimax gain:
the earlier unrestricted-class lower bound still applies. Independent
artificial Gaussian splitting of one observation is valid with
$\tau_1=\tau_2=\sqrt2\tau$; using both halves at scale $\tau$ is invalid.

### Why the first-order repair does not solve the original problem

For the A2 construction, if $\min_k\eta_k\ge q\tau_2$, where
$q=z_{1-(\alpha-\delta)/2}$, no projected candidate improves the smaller
of the untruncated direct and norm-only radii. In fact, nonzero $R_k$
have $d_k\ge\eta_k$, so triangle inequalities and nuclear/Frobenius norm
comparison give $B\ge\min(M,\min_k\eta_k)\|R\|_F$. Hence its radius is at
least $\min(M,q\tau_2)(\|PL\|_F+\|R\|_F)$, which is at least
$\min(M,q\tau_2)\|L\|_F$. The explicit envelopes meet this condition in
the equal-noise experiments below. This is a proved limitation of this
particular repair, not a universal computational lower bound.

title: The adaptation obstruction at an arbitrary orientation
label: A3
statement:
Let a base tensor $A_0$ have norm $a<M$, and leave at least one unused unit
of every supplied Tucker or TT rank cap. Choose mode subspaces $W_k$ such
that $A_0$ is orthogonal to every tensor in
$\mathcal W=\bigotimes_k W_k$. One sufficient choice is to take at least
one $W_k$ orthogonal to the column space of $A_{0,(k)}$. Put
$M_0=\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$ and $L_{\mathcal W}=P_{\mathcal W}L$.
Then

$$\mathbb E_{A_0}|C|\ge c_\alpha\min(M_0,\tau)\rho(L_{\mathcal W})$$

for every interval honest on the outer class. If the restriction of the
loading to an $m$-dimensional orthogonal diagonal block in $\mathcal W$
equals $b$ times a flat unit loading, the stronger bound is

$$\mathbb E_{A_0}|C|\ge c_{K,\alpha}|b|\,
\mathfrak r_K(m,M_0,\tau).$$

Here $\rho$ is taken within the indicated product subspace. The zero
overlap case gives a zero lower bound and says nothing further.

**Proof.** Add rank-one perturbations $B\in\mathcal W$ with norm at most
$M_0$. Rank subadditivity keeps $A_0+B$ in every outer unfolding cap;
orthogonality gives $\|A_0+B\|_F^2=a^2+\|B\|_F^2\le M^2$.
Translate the Gaussian experiment by $A_0$. The target difference is
$\langle L_{\mathcal W},B\rangle$. Apply the two-point construction of L1
or the existing flat-loading mixtures, all of which have rank one.
Unused observed coordinates contain identical independent Gaussian noise
under both hypotheses and do not change the likelihood calculation.
This is a rotation-invariant extension of the preceding block-supported
shifted bound, not a complete characterization at every mean.

title: A cap-valid tangent interval on the original unseparated class
label: A4
statement:
There is a more useful repair when mode caps $\bar r_k\le p_k$ are supplied.
Use the same independent Gaussian pilot and validation data and envelopes
as A2. Let $Q_k$ project onto the leading $\bar r_k$ pilot left singular
vectors. Define

$$e_k=\begin{cases}
0,&\bar r_k=p_k,\\
\min\{1,2\eta_k/(\sigma_{\bar r_k}(Z^{(1)}_{(k)})-\eta_k)\},
&\bar r_k<p_k,\ \sigma_{\bar r_k}(Z^{(1)}_{(k)})>\eta_k,\\
1,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}$$

With the first-order product-space projector from the previous stage,

$$T=\bigotimes_k Q_k+\sum_k(I-Q_k)\otimes\bigotimes_{l\ne k}Q_l,$$

put $R=(I-T)L$ and

$$B_T=M\|R\|_F\min\{1,(\sum_{k<l}e_k^2e_l^2)^{1/2}\}.$$

The interval centered at $\langle TL,Z^{(2)}\rangle$, with radius
$B_T+q\tau_2\|TL\|_F$, is honest on **every** tensor with these supplied
mode caps and norm bound, including zero, arbitrarily weak signals, and
actual ranks strictly below the caps. No singular-value separation is
assumed. Choose the smallest pilot-measurable radius among this candidate,
the direct interval, and the structural norm interval, as before.

**Proof.** Let $V_k$ be the actual left singular subspace of $A_{(k)}$.
On the simultaneous noise event we claim
$\|(I-Q_k)P_{V_k}\|_{op}\le e_k$. This is immediate for $e_k=1$ or
$Q_k=I$. Otherwise $\sigma_{\bar r_k}(Z^{(1)}_{(k)})>\eta_k$ forces
the true mode rank to equal the supplied cap: a smaller true rank would
give that observed singular value at most $\eta_k$ by Weyl's inequality.
The pilot tail after the cap is at most $\eta_k$, so
$\|(I-Q_k)A_{(k)}\|_{op}\le2\eta_k$. Multiplying by the inverse nonzero
singular values and using
$\sigma_{\bar r_k}(A_{(k)})\ge
\sigma_{\bar r_k}(Z^{(1)}_{(k)})-\eta_k$ proves the claim.

Decompose $A$ into the mutually orthogonal mode-projector blocks indexed by
which modes fall in $I-Q_k$. The complement of $T$ consists of blocks with
at least two such modes. Counting each block once is bounded by counting
it for every contained pair. Consequently

$$\|(I-T)A\|_F^2\le\sum_{k<l}
\|(I-Q_k)(I-Q_l)A\|_F^2
\le M^2\sum_{k<l}e_k^2e_l^2.$$

The last inequality restricts each operator to its true mode subspace and
uses that operators on distinct modes commute. Combine with the trivial
bound $\|(I-T)A\|_F\le M$ and Cauchy--Schwarz against $R$.
Conditional Gaussian validation and the common pilot event now prove
coverage and valid radius selection exactly as in A2.

This algorithm is polynomial and honest for the original weak-signal
class. Strong signals can make the second-order bias correction small,
even though separation is not a coverage assumption. It is **not** a
polynomial weak-signal minimax solution or a method of estimating actual
rank. At smaller actual ranks, the unresolved cap singular values trigger
conservative error bounds. For a supplied TT cap vector, valid mode caps
are $\min(p_k,\bar r_{k-1}\bar r_k)$, with boundary TT ranks one;
the interval does not estimate TT bond ranks. Artificial splitting must
use its increased noise scales.

For the original single observation, `single_observation_interval` creates
$Z\pm\tau G'$ with independent artificial $G'$, uses scales
$\sqrt2\tau$ and error $\alpha/2$ for the cap-valid construction, and
intersects with the direct interval based on $Z$ at error $\alpha/2$.
The union bound proves honesty at error $\alpha$ despite the dependence
between these two intervals. The direct component caps the reported
length at $2z_{1-\alpha/4}\tau\|L\|_F$. The split is randomization within
the original experiment, not an extra observed replicate.

title: Sharp growing-cap rates with a polynomial algorithm
label: G1
statement:
Let $r=\min(p,\min_k\bar r_k)$, where the minimum is over the supplied
constrained unfoldings (Tucker modes or TT cuts). Suppose
$r\ge c\sqrt p$ for a fixed $c>0$. Uniformly over all remaining caps,
all $p$, and every $M,\tau>0$,

$$\mathcal L_0\asymp_{\alpha,c}\mathcal L_{\max}
\asymp_{\alpha,c}\min\{M\sqrt{r/p},\tau\}.$$

Minimax squared risk has the square of this rate. The constants do not
depend on growing ranks or tensor order. Choose deterministically between
the structural interval $[-h_0,h_0]$, $h_0=M\sqrt{r/p}$, and the direct
Gaussian interval centered at $\psi(Z)$ with radius $z_{1-\alpha/2}\tau$.
This takes $O(p)$ accessed entries and arithmetic for the coordinate loading.
For a rotated flat loading, obtaining the contractions has its additional
polynomial input-access cost. No factor estimation or exponential scan is
required.

**Upper proof.** An unfolding attaining the smallest cap has loading matrix
singular values $1/\sqrt p$, repeated $p$ times. Matrix singular-value
duality and Cauchy--Schwarz bound its contraction with any rank-at-most-$r$
matrix of norm $M$ by $M\sqrt{r/p}$. Thus the structural interval covers
surely. The direct error is $N(0,\tau^2)$. Deterministic radius selection
proves the length upper bound. Choosing estimator zero when $h_0\le\tau$
and the direct estimator otherwise gives squared risk at most
$\min(h_0^2,\tau^2)$.

**Lower proof.** For a uniform size-$r$ subset $S$ of $\{1,\ldots,p\}$ set

$$A_S=b\sum_{i\in S}E_i,\qquad
b=\min\{M/\sqrt r,\tau\sqrt{\log(1+p/(4r^2))}\}.$$

All constrained unfolding ranks are $r$, the norm is at most $M$, and the
common target is $\Delta=rb/\sqrt p$. For independent supports $S,T$,
the full Gaussian likelihood second moment equals
$\mathbb E\exp\{b^2|S\cap T|/\tau^2\}$. To bound it, for
$H=|S\cap T|$ factorial moments give
$\mathbb E\binom Hj=\binom rj(r)_j/(p)_j\le\binom rj(r/p)^j$.
Expand $(1+t)^H$ at $t=e^{b^2/\tau^2}-1$ to obtain

$$1+\chi^2(Q,P_0)\le(1+rt/p)^r\le\exp(r^2t/p)\le e^{1/4}.$$

Put $x=p/(4r^2)\le1/(4c^2)$. Since
$x/(1+x)\le\log(1+x)\le x$,

$$\frac{\tau}{2\sqrt{1+1/(4c^2)}}
\le\frac{\tau r}{\sqrt p}\sqrt{\log(1+p/(4r^2))}\le\frac\tau2.$$

Consequently $\Delta\asymp_c\min(M\sqrt{r/p},\tau)$.
Total variation is at most
$\eta=\sqrt{e^{1/4}-1}/2<1/2$.
Coverage of both zero and the common target implies
$\mathbb E_0|C|\ge\Delta(1-2\alpha-\eta)$, which is positive for
$\alpha<1/4$. The nearest-target testing argument also gives squared risk
at least $\Delta^2(1-\eta)/8$. This proves all claims.

This closes the large-cap regime using the earlier sparse-diagonal lower
bound. It is a consequence of that bound with a newly matched upper bound,
not a new sparse-mixture technique. Under $M=\tau\sqrt p$ the rate is
$\tau$, so the vanishing fixed-cap improvement has already disappeared
by rank order $\sqrt p$, well below unrestricted rank $p$.

title: General adaptation across positive growing caps is impossible
label: G2
statement:
Set $M=\tau\sqrt p$ and let the outer smallest cap satisfy
$r\ge c\sqrt p$. Every interval honest on that outer class has
$\mathbb E_0|C|\ge c_{\alpha,c}\tau$. For a fixed positive inner cap
vector, the previously established oracle minimax rate is

$$\mathfrak r_K(p)=\frac\tau{\sqrt p}
\begin{cases}(\log(ep))^{3/2},&K=3,\\
\sqrt{\log(ep)},&K\ge4.
\end{cases}$$

Zero belongs to every such inner class. Its worst-case expected length
under outer honesty is therefore at least order $\tau$, a diverging factor
$\sqrt p/(\log(ep))^{3/2}$ or $\sqrt{p/\log(ep)}$ larger than its
known-class oracle rate. No algorithm, including an exponential one, can
be simultaneously minimax in rate over these positive fixed and growing
cap classes. This is stronger than excluding only the known-rank-zero
oracle. It does not conflict with earlier adaptation across *fixed* outer
caps, whose constants were allowed to depend on that outer cap.

**Nonzero version.** Suppose $A_0$ is supported on the first $q$ coordinates
in every mode, with norm $a<M$ and actual constrained ranks $r_{0,k}$.
Let $m=p-q$, $s=\min(m,\min_k(\bar r_k-r_{0,k}))$ and
$M_0=\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$. If $s\ge c\sqrt m$, then

$$\mathbb E_{A_0}|C|\gtrsim_{\alpha,c}
\min\{M_0\sqrt{s/p},\tau\sqrt{m/p}\}.$$

**Proof.** Add the G1 alternatives on the disjoint remaining block. Norm
squares add; every unfolding rank increases by at most $s$. Translation
by $A_0$ preserves Gaussian likelihood overlaps, and normalization of the
target multiplies the dimension-$m$ lower bound by $\sqrt{m/p}$.
This gives a positive nonzero-base obstruction when weak extra rank fits
inside the supplied caps. Arbitrarily oriented versions follow by using
orthogonal product blocks when the transformed loading is flat on that block.

title: A dyadic loading bound using the full weight profile
label: W1
statement:
Return to a prescribed orthogonal product loading
$L_w=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i U_i$, with decreasing absolute weights and fixed
positive caps. The ambient mode dimensions may exceed $m$.
Partition the ordered indices into $B_0=\{1\}$ and
$B_j=\{2^{j-1}+1,\ldots,\min(2^j,m)\}$ for $j\ge1$, stopping when empty.
Let $a_j=\max_{i\in B_j}|w_i|$, $d_j=|B_j|$, and
$\alpha_j=\alpha/2^{j+1}$. Define

$$H_K(w)=\sum_j a_j(j+1)^{\nu_K},\qquad
\nu_3=3/2,\quad \nu_K=1/2\ (K\ge4).$$

There is a full-data honest interval satisfying the deterministic bound

$$|C_w|\le C_{K,\bar r,\alpha}
\min\{M\|w\|_\infty,\tau H_K(w)\}.$$

The minimax squared risk is at most a constant times the square of the
same expression. This is a statistical upper bound using the ideal block
residual fits, not a polynomial implementation of those fits.

**Proof.** Rotate the known orthogonal factors into coordinates. Restrict
the data to each $d_j^K$ block; this cannot increase its norm or rank caps.
Apply the earlier weighted residual confidence projection at error
$\alpha_j$. With $J_2=J(2\bar r)$, its block diameter is at most

$$4J_2^{K/2}a_j\sum_{s=1}^{d_j}\lambda_s^{(j)}s^{-K/2},$$

where

$$\lambda_s^{(j)}=\tau\sqrt{2\{s\log(ed_j/s)+Ks\log(1+4K)
+\log(2d_j/\alpha_j)\}}.$$

For $s\ge1$, $\log(ed_j)$ and $\log(1/\alpha_j)$ are bounded by a fixed
constant times $j+1$. Thus
$\lambda_s^{(j)}\le C_{K,\alpha}\tau\sqrt{s(j+1)}$.
The remaining sum is harmonic for $K=3$, bounded by $C(j+1)$, and bounded
by a $K$-dependent constant for $K\ge4$. Add the block intervals and use
$\sum_j\alpha_j\le\alpha$. Their lengths sum to at most $C\tau H_K(w)$.
The old structural radius is at most $M\sqrt{\min\bar r_k}\|w\|_\infty$,
which is $O(M\|w\|_\infty)$ for fixed caps. Select the smaller deterministic
bound before seeing the data.

For squared error use block residual fits with error budgets
$\beta_j=2^{-j-4}$ and deterministic optimization tolerance $\tau$.
The earlier excess-tail proof gives each block error an $L_2$ norm at most
$C\tau a_j(j+1)^{\nu_K}$: the deterministic diameter term has the bound
just derived, and the excess term has $L_2$ norm $O(\tau a_j)$ because
$\sum_s s^{-K/2}<\infty$ and $\mathbb E T_{0,j}^2\le2\beta_j\tau^2$.
Minkowski's inequality bounds the $L_2$ norm of their summed error by
$C\tau H_K(w)$, without requiring independence. Compare with estimator
zero and its structural risk bound. The finite number of blocks makes
measurability and summation immediate.

title: Sharp rates at every budget for polynomially decreasing loadings
label: W2
statement:
Suppose for fixed $\beta>0$ and $C_0<\infty$ that the nonzero, decreasing
weights satisfy

$$|w_i|\le C_0|w_1|i^{-\beta},\qquad i=1,\ldots,m.$$

For fixed positive caps and order, uniformly over all $m,M,\tau>0$,

$$\mathcal L_0(\Theta;L_w)\asymp\mathcal L_{\max}(\Theta;L_w)
\asymp |w_1|\min(M,\tau),$$

and minimax squared risk is $\asymp |w_1|^2\min(M,\tau)^2$.
Constants may depend on $\beta,C_0,K,\bar r,\alpha$, but not on dimension
or budget. This includes all signed power-law weights, whether normalized
or not. In particular, $0<\beta<1/2$ permits diffuse unit-Frobenius
loadings with $|w_1|\to0$; the result is not limited to a constant product
overlap with a unit-Frobenius loading.

**Proof.** For $j\ge1$,
$a_j\le C_0|w_1|2^{-\beta(j-1)}$. The series
$\sum_j2^{-\beta(j-1)}(j+1)^{\nu_K}$ is finite for every fixed $\beta>0$.
W1 therefore gives the matching length and risk upper bounds. For the
lower bounds compare zero with $tU_1$, where
$t=\min(M,\tau)/2$ and its sign agrees with $w_1$. These rank-one means
belong to every positive cap class, their target difference is $t|w_1|$,
and their total variation is at most $2\Phi(1/4)-1<1/4$.
The common-target interval argument and two-point squared-loss argument
give the asserted lower orders. No lower power-envelope assumption on the
other weights is needed.

As $\beta\downarrow0$ the constants deteriorate: the dyadic sum is of
order at most $1+\beta^{-(\nu_K+1)}$ up to fixed constants. Thus this
theorem does not cover a dimension-dependent exponent approaching zero
uniformly, and does not contradict the extra logarithmic factors for
flat loadings. Completely arbitrary unequal weight sequences, including
many slowly varying profiles, remain uncharacterized.

**Nonorthogonal perturbations.** Suppose $L=L_w+R$, with the same weight
condition and a known otherwise arbitrary tensor $R$ satisfying
$\|R\|_F\le\epsilon|w_1|$ for a fixed $0\le\epsilon<1$.
The same sharp rates hold with constants depending also on $1-\epsilon$.
For the lower bound,
$|\langle L,U_1\rangle|\ge(1-\epsilon)|w_1|$.
For large budgets add a direct interval for $\langle R,A\rangle$ at a
separate error allocation, costing $O(\tau\|R\|_F)$.
For small budgets, $\rho(L_w)=|w_1|$ by generalized Hölder and
$\rho(R)\le\|R\|_F$; the canonical expansion bounds the structural
radius by $\sqrt J M(1+\epsilon)|w_1|$. The same reasoning applies to
squared error, using the direct residual estimator and Minkowski.
This gives an all-budget result for a class of loadings without an exact
orthogonal representation, but is not a theorem for every loading.

title: A restricted computational separation for these newly matched loadings
label: W3
statement:
The W2 rate does not automatically have an efficient estimator. To make
this distinction precise, let $w_i=w_1i^{-\beta}>0$ with fixed
$0<\beta<1/K$, and set $M=\tau\sqrt p$.
Choose constants

$$\frac1K<a<\min\left\{\frac12,\frac{1-2\beta}{K-2}\right\},
\qquad 0<b<a-\frac1K.$$

For $s=\lfloor p^a\rfloor$ and $D=\lfloor p^b\rfloor$, every polynomial
estimator of total degree at most $D$ in the full observed tensor has
worst-case squared risk polynomially larger than the unrestricted
$\tau^2w_1^2$ rate of W2.

**Finite statement and proof.** For a uniform size-$s$ support $S$, put
$x_S=s^{-1/2}\mathbf1_S$ and let $D_w$ be the diagonal map with entries
$w_p/w_i\le1$. Use the rank-one alternatives

$$A_S=\tau\lambda(D_wx_S)\otimes x_S^{\otimes(K-1)},\qquad
0<\tau\lambda\le M.$$

They have norm at most $M$ and common weighted target
$\Delta=\tau\lambda w_p s^{1-K/2}$.
All factors are nonnegative, so for two supports
$0\le\langle A_S,A_T\rangle/\tau^2\le
\lambda^2|S\cap T|^K/s^K$.
The full Gaussian Hermite expansion therefore bounds the squared norm of
the centered likelihood ratio through degree $D$ by

$$\chi^2_{\le D}\le\sum_{d=1}^D
\frac{\lambda^{2d}\mathbb E H^{Kd}}{d!s^{Kd}}
\le\frac{\mu e^\mu B_D}{1-B_D}=\eta_D^2,
\quad \mu=s^2/p,\quad B_D=\frac{\lambda^2(KD)^K}{s^K}<1.$$

For completeness, counting maps by their nonempty fibers gives
$H^q=\sum_{j=1}^q S(q,j)(H)_j$, where $S(q,j)$ counts partitions of $q$
elements into $j$ nonempty sets. We have $S(q,j)\le j^q/j!$ and
$\mathbb E(H)_j\le\mu^j$.
Hence $\mathbb E H^q\le q^q(e^\mu-1)\le\mu e^\mu q^q$.
Substitute $q=Kd$ and sum the geometric upper bound to get the display.
For a degree-$D$ estimator with worst-case squared risk $R$, orthogonality
of Hermite polynomials and Cauchy--Schwarz give
$|\mathbb E_QT-\mathbb E_0T|\le\sqrt R\,\eta_D$.
The two target means differ by $\Delta$ and their estimation biases are
each at most $\sqrt R$, so

$$R\ge\Delta^2/(2+\eta_D)^2.$$

Set $\lambda=\sqrt p$. Then $\mu\to0$ and
$B_D=O(p^{1-Ka+Kb})\to0$, whereas

$$\frac{\Delta}{\tau w_1}
\asymp p^{1/2-\beta-a(K-2)/2}\longrightarrow\infty$$

at a polynomial rate by the choice of $a$. Such an $a$ exists precisely
under the stated sufficient condition $\beta<1/K$. This proves the
restricted separation, using the earlier general low-degree argument with
a new loading-compatible prior. It includes diffuse power-law loadings
with sharp all-budget rates from W2.

This is not a lower bound for all polynomial-time algorithms or all
confidence intervals. An interval honest on zero and these alternatives
would give the test $\mathbf1\{\Delta\in C(Z)\}$ with total error at most
$2\alpha+\mathbb E_0|C|/\Delta$. Excluding such efficient tests requires
an additional computational hypothesis; the polynomial-estimator result
alone does not supply one.

title: Efficient pointwise optimality at strong saturated Tucker means
label: P1
statement:
This result concerns **Tucker mode caps all equal to $r$**, $1\le r\le p$.
It does not substitute TT bond caps for mode caps. Let

$$A_0=\sum_{i\in S}a_i E_i,\qquad |S|=r,\quad
a=\min_{i\in S}|a_i|>0,\quad
\|A_0\|_F+\tau\le M\le c_0a\sqrt r,$$

where $c_0>1$ is fixed. The support and signed amplitudes are not supplied
to the algorithm. These means saturate every supplied mode cap.
There is a polynomial interval honest on the entire unseparated Tucker
class such that, in the strong-signal regime specified below,

$$\mathbb E_{A_0}|C|\asymp_{K,\alpha,c_0}\tau\sqrt{r/p},$$

and this matches the infimum expected length at $A_0$ under that *same
outer-class honesty requirement*. Both $p$ and $r$ may grow. This is
pointwise optimality in rate, not optimal leading constants.

**Algorithm and noise budgets.** Make the valid artificial split
$Z^{(1)}=Z+\tau G'$, $Z^{(2)}=Z-\tau G'$, with independent errors of scale
$v=\sqrt2\tau$. Set $\delta=\alpha r/(8p)$ and

$$\eta=2v\sqrt{2\{(p+p^{K-1})\log9+\log(2K/\delta)\}}.$$

Use the preceding cap-valid tangent interval with pilot failure budget
$\delta$ and total failure budget $\alpha/2$. Its validation quantile is
$q=z_{1-(\alpha/2-\delta)/2}$. Intersect it with the direct interval on
$Z$ at error $\alpha/2$ and the structural range. All choices are valid on
the unseparated class. The total reported length is bounded by
$2z_{1-\alpha/4}\tau$, including on pilot failure.

A sufficient condition for the pointwise rate is

$$a\ge 4\eta,\qquad a\ge \eta^2\sqrt p/\tau.$$

For fixed order/confidence this is satisfied at sufficiently large constant
multiple of $\tau p^{K-1/2}$. This requirement is conservative and much
stronger than a claim of optimal computational signal strength.

**Upper proof.** On the simultaneous pilot event, the top-$r$ projector
$Q_k$ satisfies $\|Q_k-P_k\|_{op}\le d=4\eta/a$, where $P_k$ projects
onto the coordinates in $S$. The cap-valid certificate has each angle
bound at most $d$ by Weyl's inequality and $a\ge4\eta$.
Write $T_Q$ and $T_P$ for their first-order product-space projectors.
The representation

$$T_Q=\sum_k\bigotimes_{l\ne k}Q_l-(K-1)\bigotimes_l Q_l$$

with an identity in the omitted mode, and product telescoping, gives
$\|T_Q-T_P\|_{op}\le2K(K-1)d$.
For the diagonal loading,
$T_PL=p^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in S}E_i$, so

$$\|T_QL\|_F\le\sqrt{r/p}+2K(K-1)d.$$

The cap-valid bias is bounded by
$M\sqrt{\binom K2}d^2\le
16c_0\sqrt{\binom K2}\sqrt r\,\eta^2/a$.
The assumed amplitude makes this $O(\tau\sqrt{r/p})$.
It also gives $d\le4\tau/(\eta\sqrt p)=O(\sqrt{r/p})$, because
$\eta\gtrsim\tau$ and $r\ge1$. Thus the selected/intersected interval
has length $O(\tau\sqrt{r/p})$ on the pilot event. Off that event its
length is $O(\tau)$, with probability at most
$\delta=O(r/p)\le O(\sqrt{r/p})$. The expected-length upper bound follows.
The dimension-dependent failure budget is essential to this argument;
fixed failure probability would leave an unjustified $O(\tau)$ term.

**Lower proof.** Put $V=r^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in S}E_i$ and compare $A_0$ with
$A_0+(\tau/2)V$. Both have mode ranks at most $r$ and norms at most $M$.
Their full Gaussian total variation is less than $1/4$ and their target
difference is $(\tau/2)\sqrt{r/p}$. The common-target interval argument
at base $A_0$ proves the lower bound. This lower comparison uses the same
outer class on which the algorithm is honest.

**Computation.** Economy SVDs of the $p\times p^{K-1}$ unfoldings require
$O(Kp^{K+1})$ arithmetic and $O(p^K+p^2)$ working storage for fixed $K$.
Tensor projection has polynomial cost of the same order. The new code
uses economy SVDs; the previous prototype requested full right singular
matrices, which could allocate $p^{2K-2}$ entries. Thus the implementation
now scales with the explicit tensor rather than that avoidable allocation.
It still reads the full tensor and does not claim sublinear access cost.
